confirmed.title: Budget/failure truncation of the Wikipedia summary loop silently turns an AMBIGUOUS same-title set into a confident single pick
confirmed.description: `lookup_wikipedia` collects up to 3 matching pages, fetches a summary for each, and hands the SUCCESSFULLY FETCHED ones to `_select_context_candidate`. But `_lookup_json` returns None both when the per-batch call budget is exhausted and after two consecutive transport failures — and nothing tells the selector that pages were skipped. `_select_context_candidate`'s single-candidate branch is far more permissive than its multi-candidate branch (`return item if score >= 0` vs `best > 0 and len(winners) == 1`), so losing the 2nd and 3rd summaries converts "three same-title works, refuse" into "one candidate, accept at score 0". The ambiguity evidence is `len(pages)`, but the decision uses `len(candidates)`. This directly contradicts the function's own contract ("unresolved ambiguity stays missing") and the module docstring ("honest-missing beats a confident wrong match"), and the wrong value is then stored as a `lookup:` fact and shown to the boss as «нашла».
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:831-849 —
    candidates = []
    for page in pages[:3]:
        summary = _lookup_json(base + "/api/rest_v1/page/summary/"
                               + quote(page.replace(" ", "_"), safe=""), budget)
        if isinstance(summary, dict):
            candidates.append((page, summary))
    chosen = _select_context_candidate(candidates, entry, ...)

media.py:732-742 —
    scored = [(item, _candidate_score(blob(item), entry)) for item in candidates]
    if len(scored) == 1:
        ...
        return item if score >= 0 else None

media.py:609-614 — `_lookup_json` returns None on BOTH `not budget.allow()` and FetchError, indistinguishably from "page had no summary".
confirmed.suggestion: Make the selector see the ambiguity that was never resolved. Either pass `len(pages[:3])` into `_select_context_candidate` and refuse whenever `len(candidates) < n_matching_pages and n_matching_pages > 1`, or have `_lookup_json` return a distinguishable sentinel for "skipped/failed" so `lookup_wikipedia` can bail with `{}` rather than fall into the single-candidate branch. Same reasoning applies to `lookup_openlibrary` if its `limit=5` is ever truncated.

confirmed.title: A photo-visible Russian creator now VETOES the correct lookup instead of confirming it
confirmed.description:
`_candidate_score` scores a photo-visible creator by exact WORD-SET membership: all name tokens present → +12, otherwise → −12. Russian Wikipedia writes creators in oblique cases («роман Михаила Булгакова») and OpenLibrary often transliterates them, so for a Russian cover the photo's «Михаил Булгаков» produces tokens {михаил, булгаков} while the candidate's word set is {михаила, булгакова} — no overlap, −12. On the single-candidate path `return item if score >= 0 else None` then rejects the CORRECT page, and `_strong_context_terms`' first branch vetoes it a second time on the same mismatch.

This is an interaction: d31f2ba wrote the ±12 rule against SUBSTRING containment (`if w in low`), where 'булгаков' matched inside 'булгакова' and the genitive suffix was tolerated. 41e1153's word-set fix (correct in itself — it stopped «АСТ» matching inside «фантастика») removed that tolerance without re-tuning the creator rule.

The common shape is exactly the one the feature targets: a book cover printing author + title with no year and no genre. `enrich_entries` runs the lookups because year/genre are missing, the visible author guarantees they return nothing, and the 2–5 calls consumed come out of the shared 10-call batch budget — starving later entries for a guaranteed-zero result.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:697-701 —
    creator = (entry.get("creator") or "") if entry.get("creator_src") == "photo" else ""
    creator_terms = [w for w in _WORD_RE.findall(creator.casefold())
                     if w not in _CONTEXT_STOP]
    if creator_terms:
        score += 12 if all(w in words for w in creator_terms) else -12

where media.py:691 `words = set(_WORD_RE.findall(str(blob or "").casefold()))` — exact tokens only.
confirmed.suggestion: Match creator tokens by stem rather than by identity on the Cyrillic path: compare on a prefix basis (e.g. a candidate token that startswith the photo token, or the first ~5 chars) so 'булгаков' matches 'булгакова' but 'фантастика' still cannot be matched by 'аст' (the prefix must come from the NAME token, not from an arbitrary substring). Alternatively make the penalty asymmetric — keep +12 for a confirmed match but use 0 rather than −12 for a non-match on a `_wiki_lang(title) == "ru"` lookup, where declension makes absence uninformative.

confirmed.title: `_strong_context_terms` treats any two ordinary comment words as a veto, rejecting correct unique matches
confirmed.description:
The third branch returns `terms if len(terms) >= 2`, so ANY photo comment containing two words of ≥3 letters that are not in `_CONTEXT_STOP` becomes veto-strength context. `_select_context_candidate` then discards a lone same-title candidate unless one of those words appears verbatim in it. The docstring states a much higher bar — «a platform, explicit photo field, or multi-word identifier is useful; a one-word review such as «топ» is not» — but the code does not implement "identifier", only "two words".

Comments are free prose transcribed off the photo, and the extract prompt actively asks for them («preserve concise visible context…»). Ordinary two-word comments — «смотрели вместе», «экранизация романа», «подарок брата» — almost never recur verbatim in a Wikipedia summary, so they veto an otherwise unambiguous, correct page and the entry falls to the model fallback labelled «по памяти», after burning 2 lookup calls. The stronger the boss's photo context, the worse the outcome — the inverse of the intent.
confirmed.suggestion: Restrict the veto to context that actually identifies a work: platform terms, a photo-visible year, a photo-visible creator, or a capitalized/proper-noun run in the comment — not merely two content words. Everything else should influence the SCORE (which already handles it) without carrying a veto. As written, the veto only makes the single-candidate path stricter than the multi-candidate path in the one case where a single candidate is most likely correct.

confirmed.title: A tie among candidates that AGREE is treated as unresolvable ambiguity
confirmed.description:
The multi-candidate branch requires a UNIQUE top scorer (`len(winners) == 1`). It never asks whether the tied candidates actually disagree about the field being extracted. OpenLibrary's `search.json` routinely returns several docs whose titles normalize identically — editions/duplicate work records of the SAME book, with the SAME author and year — so a book whose photo-visible author CONFIRMS every candidate scores +12 across the board, ties, and yields `{}`.

This is a regression against 41a5818, which took the first exact-title match and got the right answer. d31f2ba raised `limit=3` to `limit=5`, which makes duplicate-title collisions strictly more likely, and then made any collision fatal. Net effect: for common books the OpenLibrary path spends a call and returns nothing, and the field falls to the model as «по памяти» — a worse source presented with a weaker provenance, for a work the lookup unambiguously identified.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:743-745 —
    best = max(score for _, score in scored)
    winners = [item for item, score in scored if score == best]
    return winners[0] if best > 0 and len(winners) == 1 else None

media.py:755-763 — `limit=5` and `candidates = [doc for doc in docs[:5] if isinstance(doc, dict) and normalize_title(doc.get("title")) == norm]` admits every same-title edition as a rival.
confirmed.suggestion: Resolve per FIELD rather than per candidate: when the tied top-scoring candidates all yield the same normalized value for a field, that field is unambiguous — keep it. Only fields on which the winners disagree should stay missing. That preserves the "honest-missing beats a wrong match" rule (a genuine same-title conflict still refuses) while recovering the duplicate-edition case, which is the dominant one for books.

confirmed.title: A negated removal still removes: «не удаляй №2» deletes card entry 2
confirmed.description:
`parse_correction` detects the removal intent with a bare substring scan and no negation handling, while the kind words next to it get full negation handling via `_kind_named`. So «не удаляй №2» sets `remove=True`, `_NUM_RE` finds 2, and the function returns `("remove", [2])` — `resolve_media_correction` then drops exactly the entry the boss asked her to keep and re-shows the card as if he had requested it. «Не убирай №2, убери №3» removes BOTH.

Nothing is stored at that point, so no catalog row is damaged — but the entry is gone from the staged set, and the boss's next «да» silently saves less than he approved; recovering it means re-sending the photo. There is no test for a negated remove (`test_parse_correction_remove` covers only the affirmative forms), and the parallel `test_parse_correction_kind_flip_respects_negation` shows the negation contract was intended to apply to corrections generally.

Origin is 41a5818, but d31f2ba is where `_kind_negated` was introduced and applied only to the kind vocabularies, leaving the asymmetry in place and unremarked.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:1259-1261 —
    remove = any(w in low for w in _REMOVE_WORDS)
    movie = _kind_named(low, _MOVIE_WORDS)
    book = _kind_named(low, _BOOK_WORDS)

Compare media.py:1197-1204, `_kind_named`, which walks each occurrence and skips any preceded by `_NEGATION_RE`. `_REMOVE_WORDS = ("убер", "убра", "удал", "выкин", "выброс", "remove", "drop ", "delete")` — «не удаляй» contains "удал".
confirmed.suggestion: Route the removal detection through the same helper as the kinds: `remove = _kind_named(low, _REMOVE_WORDS)`, and treat `_kind_negated(low, _REMOVE_WORDS)` with an explicit entry reference as `None` (route it) rather than as a removal. Add the negated forms to `test_parse_correction_remove`.

confirmed.title: A manual kind correction destroys photo-visible fields; only the caption path preserves them
confirmed.description:
`media.clear_enrichment` pops every entry in `FIELDS` regardless of provenance, including values whose `_src` is "photo". `force_kind` compensates: it snapshots the photo-sourced values into `seen` and re-appends them to the comment before clearing, so the visible evidence survives as honest photo context. The correction path does NOT — `resolve_media_correction` calls `clear_enrichment` bare.

So when the boss photographs a cover printing «Иван Ефремов · 1957 · фантастика», sees the card show all three «на фото», and replies «это фильм», all three are destroyed. The year and genre were kind-independent facts read off the photo; they are re-derived by a lookup/model pass and re-labelled «нашла»/«по памяти», and the entry loses the comment terms that would have disambiguated the new lookup (`_context_terms` now has nothing to work with, which also makes finding #1 more likely to fire on that entry).

This is an interaction defect: at 41a5818 `clear_enrichment` was correct, because `extract` produced no structured photo fields — only lookup/model ones, which a kind flip genuinely invalidates. d31f2ba added photo-sourced `creator`/`year`/`genre` to `extract` (`_photo_field`) without revisiting this call site; 41e1153 then built the preservation logic in `force_kind` only.
confirmed.evidence:
tg_ingest_agent.py:4460-4467 —
                if entries[i - 1]["kind"] != action:
                    entries[i - 1]["kind"] = action
                    flipped.append(media.clear_enrichment(entries[i - 1]))

media.py:968-974 —
    for f in FIELDS:
        entry.pop(f, None)
        entry.pop(f + "_src", None)

versus media.py:368-374 in `force_kind`, which snapshots `seen` first and folds it back into `comment`.
confirmed.suggestion: Move the snapshot-into-comment step out of `force_kind` into a shared helper (or into `clear_enrichment` itself, guarded by a flag) and use it from `resolve_media_correction`, so both flip paths preserve visible evidence identically. Better still, only clear fields whose meaning is kind-dependent — `creator` — and keep a photo-sourced `year`/`genre`, which do not change when a work is reclassified.

confirmed.title: A visible genre outside the fixed vocabulary is silently dropped and can be replaced by a model guess
confirmed.description:
`_photo_field` runs a photo-read genre through `_genre_of`, which returns "" for anything not in `_GENRES`. The table has no вестерн, нуар, киберпанк, мюзикл, военный, сатира, western, noir, musical, war or satire. A poster plainly printing «Вестерн» therefore produces no genre at all: the card reports it under «не нашла: жанр», and the model fallback may then fill an unrelated genre shown as «жанр: драма (по памяти)» — a guess standing where the photo gave a fact.

The vocabulary gate is right for LOOKUP text (it is what stops a crafted summary planting arbitrary content), but for a photo read the value is already `_clean_line`d and capped at 80 chars, so the gate buys much less and costs the evidence the extract prompt explicitly asked the model to transcribe.
confirmed.suggestion: Either widen `_GENRES` with the missing common genres, or keep the photo-read genre verbatim when the vocabulary does not recognize it (it is already neutralized and capped) and reserve the vocabulary gate for lookup-derived text. At minimum, do not let a model guess occupy a field whose photo-visible value was discarded — suppress the model fill for `genre` when `_photo_field` saw text it could not map.

confirmed.title: d31f2ba removed the photo-comment/field-label guard, letting a comment fact outrank a real lookup fact
confirmed.description:
41a5818's `_CATALOG_FACT_RE` deliberately excluded `photo:` from the field-column alternation, with a comment stating the reason: a photo comment that happens to read like a field label is a transcription, not a verified value, and must never displace a real lookup fact. d31f2ba widened the pattern to `^(photo|lookup|model):` because it now emits legitimate `photo: author:` facts — and deleted the guard without replacing the ordering rule it protected.

`entry_facts` emits the free comment fact FIRST, before aliases and before the structured fields. `parse_catalog_facts` and `facts_fields` both keep the FIRST structured value per field. So a shelf photo whose transcribed comment begins with a lowercase English field label — `"author: Frank Herbert"` — is stored as `photo: author: Frank Herbert` and wins the creator column in the md export and in the merge preview over the real `lookup: author: …` fact emitted later. `merge_facts` compounds it: `fact_field` sees "author" on that comment fact, so it also purges the genuine older author fact from the note being merged into.

Low likelihood (needs a lowercase English label at the very start of a comment, and the prompt now asks for creator/year/genre as separate fields), but it is a deliberately removed guard with no replacement.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:1031-1032 —
_CATALOG_FACT_RE = re.compile(
    r"^(photo|lookup|model): (?:(author|director|year|genre): )?(.*)$", re.S)

media.py:987-1000 — `entry_facts` appends `f"photo: {entry['comment']}"` before the `f"{src}: {fact_label(...)}: …"` loop, and media.py:1046-1050 keeps `if not fields[field]` — first wins.
confirmed.suggestion: Restore the distinction structurally rather than by regex: prefix free photo context with a reserved label that cannot collide (`photo: context: …`, matching the existing `photo: alias: …` convention) so only genuinely structured facts can ever match the field alternation. That keeps d31f2ba's legitimate `photo: author:` facts working while re-closing the displacement path.

confirmed.title: A demonstrative request is swallowed as a no-op correction and never reaches the router
confirmed.description:
The no-number branch accepts a message on the strength of `_DEMONSTRATIVE_RE` alone, which the `_REQUEST_WORDS` and `_QUESTION_RE` guards 41e1153 added do not cover. «Давай посмотрим этот фильм» on a 1-entry card returns `("movie", [1])`; since the entry is already a movie, `resolve_media_correction` flips nothing, re-stages an identical card, and returns True — the boss's conversational message is consumed and never routed. On a multi-entry card the same message returns "unclear" and she answers «не поняла, какую запись поправить» to something that was not a correction at all.

`_REQUEST_WORDS` covers посовет/порекоменд/подбер/предлож/включ/поставь/скачай/закажи/купи but not посмотрим/почитаю/хочу, and `_ASSERTION_RE` is only consulted on the `asserts_single` path, not on the demonstrative path — so a demonstrative bypasses the assertion requirement the same review introduced.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:1290-1293 —
        asserts_single = n_entries == 1 and bool(_ASSERTION_RE.search(low))
        if not (contrast or asserts_single or _DEMONSTRATIVE_RE.search(low)
                or _BARE_KIND_RE.match(flat)):
            return None         # no entry reference at all -> not a correction

tg_ingest_agent.py:4459-4466 — when `entries[i-1]["kind"] == action` nothing is flipped, yet the function still re-stages and returns True.
confirmed.suggestion: Two independent cheap fixes: (a) require the demonstrative path to also satisfy the assertion test (or add посмотр/почита/хочу to `_REQUEST_WORDS`), so a demonstrative request routes; and (b) in `resolve_media_correction`, when a kind op changes nothing on any targeted entry, return False so the message routes normally instead of re-drawing an unchanged card.

confirmed.title: Kind-flip correction has no post-flip dedup — it can insert two identical catalog rows
confirmed.evidence: tg_ingest_agent.py:4457-4467 (flip, no dedup) vs 4158-4166 (force_kind + `entries = media.dedup_entries(entries)`); `_resolve_media_merges` index_cache is DB-only (4410-4419); `_media_store_entries` inserts unconditionally when `merge.get("row_id")` is falsy (4545-4562).
confirmed.suggestion: Run `entries = media.dedup_entries(entries)` after the flip loop (mirroring 4166), before `_stage_media_card`. Note the indices in `chosen` are consumed before this point, so the re-dedup is safe.

confirmed.title: A reply-correction kind flip DESTROYS visible photo evidence; force_kind preserves it
confirmed.description:
`media.force_kind` deliberately rescues the visible fields of a flipped entry into the photo comment: "The text is not lost — it moves into the photo comment, where it stays honest («на фото: …») and still disambiguates the lookup" (media.py:358-360), implemented at media.py:368-374. The reply-correction path performs the same semantic flip but calls `media.clear_enrichment` alone, which pops EVERY field regardless of provenance:

```python
def clear_enrichment(entry):
    for f in FIELDS:
        entry.pop(f, None)
        entry.pop(f + "_src", None)
```

So `photo`-sourced creator/year/genre read verbatim off the cover are discarded with no trace, and the fresh `enrich_entries` call runs WITHOUT the context that `_context_terms`/`_candidate_score` rely on to pick the right same-title work (the whole D3 mechanism).
confirmed.evidence: media.py:968-974 (`clear_enrichment` pops photo fields too) called bare at tg_ingest_agent.py:4465; contrast media.py:366-375 where `force_kind` snapshots `seen = [str(entry[f]) for f in FIELDS if entry.get(f) and entry.get(f + "_src") == "photo"]` and re-appends it to `comment` before clearing.
confirmed.suggestion: Extract the seen-field rescue from `force_kind` into a helper (e.g. `media.flip_kind(entry, kind)`) and call it from both sites, so the correction path also moves visible values into `comment` before clearing.

confirmed.title: The «Ты сказал, что это фильм» disclosure survives a correction that reverses it, so the card contradicts itself
confirmed.description:
`media_card_kind_forced` is appended to `notes` at capture time (4185-4190) and the notes list rides the stash so the batch disclosures survive a re-stage. `resolve_media_correction` passes it straight through:

```python
        self._stage_media_card(chat_id, lang, entries, stash.get("notes") or ())
```

The cap/unread/truncation/caption notes really are "facts about the batch" that stay true, but the forced-kind note is a claim about the CURRENT kind of the entries, and a correction is precisely the thing that invalidates it. Nothing removes or refreshes it. (`media_card_recheck` in `_media_confirm` has the same carryover, but its wording stays true.)
confirmed.evidence: tg_ingest_agent.py:4475 (`stash.get("notes")` passed verbatim); note produced at 4185-4190; template texts.py: «Ты сказал, что это {kind} — так и считаю, даже если обложка выглядит иначе.»
confirmed.suggestion: Drop the forced-kind note from the carried set whenever a correction changes any entry's kind — e.g. filter it out in `resolve_media_correction` when `flipped` is non-empty, or key it off the current entries rather than the capture-time caption.

confirmed.title: When two staged entries land on one note, neither card line describes the row the confirm produces
confirmed.description:
The `written` chain correctly stops the second entry from discarding the first's facts:

```python
                old = written.get(row_id, list(merge.get("base") or []))
                merged = media.merge_facts(old, facts_new)
                written[row_id] = merged
```

But the card previews were computed independently, each against the card-time snapshot `base` — `merge_preview(e, facts)` at 4418. Neither preview accounts for the sibling entry's contribution, so the per-entry «не нашла: …» lines are wrong about the final state of the shared row. This is the residual half of D4: the module comment at 4376-4382 asserts "the card displays exactly what a confirm stores", and for this path it does not.
confirmed.evidence: tg_ingest_agent.py:4534-4536 (`written` chain) vs 4417-4418 (`"fields": media.merge_preview(e, facts)` per entry, always against `base`). The scenario is explicitly acknowledged in the comment at 4522-4524 and pinned by test_assistant.py:21226, which asserts the stored facts but never asserts the card text.
confirmed.suggestion: Thread a per-row accumulator through `_resolve_media_merges` the same way `_media_store_entries` does: after computing an entry's preview, fold its facts into the working base used for the next entry that resolves to the same `row_id`.

confirmed.title: An album photo lost to a classify or download failure is not disclosed, while an extract failure is
confirmed.description:
The `unread` counter feeding `media_card_photo_unread` is incremented only in the `except llm.LLMError` around `media.extract` (4144-4146). Two other ways a photo drops out of the batch are silent:

```python
                path = self._download_photo_tmp(part, tmpdir, i)
                if path is None:
                    continue
                kind, desc = media.classify(self.cfg, self.conn, path, lang)
                classified.append({"kind": kind, "desc": desc, "path": path})
```

A failed download `continue`s without counting, and `media.classify` returns `(None, "")` on transport failure or non-JSON (media.py:219-224), after which `if c["kind"] != "media": continue` (4136) skips the photo without counting. The comment at 4176-4179 nevertheless states "the card must never imply it covers photos she couldn't read".
confirmed.evidence: tg_ingest_agent.py:4124-4129 (download/classify, no counter), 4136 (silent skip of kind=None), 4144-4146 (only extract failures counted). test_assistant.py:20880 `test_partial_album_download_failure_still_cards_readable_parts` pins the non-disclosure.
confirmed.suggestion: Count `path is None` and `kind is None` into `unread` (or a second counter) so `media_card_photo_unread` covers every photo that did not contribute.

confirmed.title: An inherited author fact is relabeled as a director on the card when the target note crossed categories
confirmed.description: `facts_fields` normalizes both `author:` and `director:` to the abstract field `creator` (media.py:1068), and `merge_preview` emits it as `out[f] = [INHERITED_SRC, inherited[f][1]]` with no record of the original label. `_media_entry_line` then chooses the display label from the CAPTURE's kind: `suffix = f + "_" + ("book" if e["kind"] == "book" else "movie")` (4354-4355). So an inherited value's role label is re-derived rather than carried, which is the one thing the INHERITED_SRC design was added to prevent for provenance.
confirmed.evidence: media.py:1068 (`field = "creator" if m.group(2) in ("author", "director") else ...`), media.py:1096, tg_ingest_agent.py:4354-4360. `merge_facts` keeps the old `author:` fact because `new_fields` is keyed on the LABEL (media.py:1018), so the stored row keeps `author:` while the card said `режиссёр:`.
confirmed.suggestion: Carry the original label out of `facts_fields`/`merge_preview` (e.g. `[INHERITED_SRC, value, label]`) and render inherited creator values with the label the note actually holds.

confirmed.title: A card whose sendMessage failed is still staged and still confirmable
confirmed.description:
`reply` returns `None` on `TelegramError` (line 306-308), but `_stage_media_card` treats that as a partial success — it skips only the `card_message_id` and still writes the stash and claims the pending slot:

```python
        result = self.reply(chat_id, card, reply_markup={...})
        stash = {"entries": entries, "notes": notes, "at": ...}
        if result and result.get("message_id"):
            stash["card_message_id"] = result["message_id"]
        store.kv_set(self.conn, f"media_capture:{chat_id}", json.dumps(stash, ...))
        if slot_ours:
            store.pending_set(self.conn, chat_id, "media_capture", {"n": len(entries)})
```

The consent invariant rests on "the card shows exactly what a confirm stores"; here no card was shown at all, yet a confirm remains reachable.
confirmed.evidence: tg_ingest_agent.py:4286-4303; `reply` error path at 306-308 returns None; `_media_confirm` only checks that the stash is non-empty (4483-4487).
confirmed.suggestion: Skip the stash/pending writes when `result` is falsy and reply with an honest failure, or store the stash but do not claim the pending slot so no text confirm can reach `_media_confirm`.

confirmed.title: force_kind's preserved photo text becomes a "strong context" veto that kills the very lookup the forcing enables
confirmed.description: When a caption flips an entry's kind, `force_kind` moves the other reading's visible values (author, year, genre) into the entry's photo comment. `_strong_context_terms` (d31f2ba) treats a comment with >=2 content words as evidence strong enough to VETO even a lone same-title lookup candidate. So the moved book-cover author/year become terms that the movie's Wikipedia summary will not contain, and `_select_context_candidate` returns None: the forced-kind lookup yields nothing and the card falls back to «не нашла: режиссёра, год, жанр» (or to a «по памяти» guess seeded from the same moved text, which can re-label the novelist as «режиссёр» through the model path force_kind was written to prevent). Before the flip the same values acted as a -10/-12 score penalty; after the flip they are cleared as fields but reinstated as a veto — the forcing is only half-applied. The existing tests hide this: test_movie_caption_outranks_the_book_shaped_cover feeds `creator: "", year: "", genre: ""`, so the comment stays empty and no strong terms exist.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:360 (force_kind docstring): "The text is not lost — it moves into the photo comment, where it stays honest («на фото: …») and still disambiguates the lookup."
media.py:368-374:
    seen = [str(entry[f]) for f in FIELDS
            if entry.get(f) and entry.get(f + "_src") == "photo"]
    clear_enrichment(entry)
    for value in seen:
        if value.casefold() not in (entry.get("comment") or "").casefold():
            entry["comment"] = ((entry.get("comment", "") + " · " + value) ...
media.py:717-722 (_strong_context_terms, reached because creator_src/year_src were just popped):
    terms = _context_terms({"comment": entry.get("comment") or "", "aliases": []})
    platforms = [term for term in terms if term in _PLATFORM_TERMS]
    return platforms or (terms if len(terms) >= 2 else [])
media.py:739-742:
    strong_terms = _strong_context_terms(entry)
    if strong_terms and not any(term in candidate_words for term in strong_terms):
        return None
Failure trace: cover reads {title: "EMPTY WORLD", kind: "book", creator: "Sam Youd", year: "1977"}, caption «Фильм» -> comment becomes "Sam Youd · 1977" -> strong_terms = ["sam","youd","1977"] -> the single candidate "Empty World (film) · 2015 British drama film · directed by Nick Hamm" contains none of them -> lookup discarded, card shows «не нашла: режиссёра, год, жанр». SOLUTION.md's claim "`media.force_kind` applies it to every entry BEFORE enrichment so the lookups run for the named kind" is therefore only half-delivered.
confirmed.suggestion: Mark the values force_kind relocates (e.g. keep them in a separate `comment_forced` key, or record the moved substring on the entry) and exclude them from `_context_terms`/`_strong_context_terms` for that entry — they are evidence about the REJECTED reading, so they must not gate the forced kind's lookup. Add a regression test with a non-empty visible creator+year on a caption-forced entry asserting the lookup still lands.

confirmed.title: «Ты сказал, что это фильм — так и считаю» survives a reply correction that flips the entry back, contradicting the card it is printed on
confirmed.description: `media_card_kind_forced` is appended to the batch `notes`, and `notes` ride the stash so the cap/unread/truncation disclosures survive a correction re-staging. But unlike those, the kind-forced line is a statement about the CURRENT kinds, not a durable fact about the batch: `resolve_media_correction` re-stages with `stash.get("notes")` unchanged, so after the boss corrects the forced entry the redrawn card shows the corrected kind AND still asserts she is taking it as the caption's kind. The same happens after «убери №N» removes the only entry the caption flipped.
confirmed.evidence:
tg_ingest_agent.py:4185-4190:
    if forced:
        notes.append(T(
            lang, "media_card_kind_forced",
            kind=T(lang, "media_kind_movie" ... )))
tg_ingest_agent.py:4475 (correction re-stage, unchanged from 41a5818):
    self._stage_media_card(chat_id, lang, entries, stash.get("notes") or ())
texts.py:224: "Ты сказал, что это {kind} — так и считаю, даже если обложка выглядит иначе."
Failure scenario: photo captioned «Фильм», vision says kind="book", force_kind flips -> card note «Ты сказал, что это фильм…». Boss replies «Не фильм, а книга» (parse_correction returns ("book",[1]) via the contrast branch). Redrawn card: «1. 📚 «EMPTY WORLD» — книга …» immediately followed by «Ты сказал, что это фильм — так и считаю, даже если обложка выглядит иначе.» No test covers a correction after a caption-forced card.
confirmed.suggestion: Don't persist the kind-forced (and identified) line in the stash notes; recompute it at render time from the caption intent vs the entries' current kinds — or drop it from `notes` before re-staging in `resolve_media_correction` when the correction touched a forced entry.

confirmed.title: A reply-correction kind flip silently discards the entry's photo-visible fields, while the caption path preserves them
confirmed.description: `clear_enrichment` pops all of creator/year/genre regardless of provenance, so the reply-correction path throws away values the boss SAW labeled «на фото» on the previous card, with no disclosure and no fallback text. `force_kind` — same user intent, expressed in a caption — deliberately keeps that text as photo context. The two paths to the identical outcome lose different amounts of evidence, and the correction path also strips the disambiguators the re-enrichment lookup would use.
confirmed.evidence:
tg_ingest_agent.py:4464-4465:
    entries[i - 1]["kind"] = action
    flipped.append(media.clear_enrichment(entries[i - 1]))
media.py:968-974 clear_enrichment pops every FIELDS entry incl. `*_src == "photo"`.
Failure scenario: exactly test_single_entry_natural_not_book_but_movie_correction's fixture (test_assistant.py:20612) — entry read with creator "ZACH BOHANNON", year "2018", genre "horror", all photo-sourced and shown on card #1. After «Не книга, а фильм» the redrawn card shows «не нашла: режиссёра, год, жанр» and no «на фото:» line: three visible facts vanished between two cards with no explanation. The test only asserts the kind line, so nothing catches it.
confirmed.suggestion: Make the correction path reuse force_kind's contract (move photo-sourced values into the comment before clearing), e.g. by extracting that preservation into a shared `_flip_kind(entry, kind)` helper used by both `force_kind` and `resolve_media_correction`.

confirmed.title: merge_preview can promise a creator the merged note will not actually surface (author/director label seam)
confirmed.description: `merge_facts` keys replacement on the raw fact LABEL (author|director|year|genre) while `facts_fields`/`parse_catalog_facts` normalize both labels to the single field `creator`. If a note in Books still carries a `…: director: X` fact (reachable when a Movies note was recategorized into Books), a fresh book capture's `…: author: Y` does not replace it: both survive, the card's merge preview shows author Y, and `parse_catalog_facts` (first structured value wins, old facts sort first) reports X in the md export and in a later card's «уже в записи» — where a stored DIRECTOR is then rendered under the «автор» label. This is the one residual case where SOLUTION.md's "`media.merge_preview` computes the fields that merge actually leaves" is not delivered.
confirmed.evidence:
media.py:1003 `_FACT_FIELD_RE = re.compile(r"^(?:photo|lookup|model): (author|director|year|genre): ")` and media.py:1018-1019:
    new_fields = {fact_field(f) for f in new} - {None}
    kept = [f for f in old if fact_field(f) not in new_fields]
vs media.py:1067-1070 (facts_fields): `field = "creator" if m.group(2) in ("author", "director") else m.group(2)`.
Failure scenario: note #12 «Дюна» captured as a movie (fact `lookup: director: Дени Вильнёв`), later recategorized to Books. A new «Дюна» book capture merges into #12 with `lookup: author: Фрэнк Герберт`; the card shows «автор: Фрэнк Герберт», the stored row keeps both facts, and «дай md по Books» prints Дени Вильнёв in the Creator column.
confirmed.suggestion: Normalize in `merge_facts` too — compare on the same field key `facts_fields` uses (map author/director -> creator) so a fresh creator fact replaces the old one whatever label it carried.

area_summaries.summary:
Audited d31f2ba's 545 unreviewed media.py lines against the CURRENT code (HEAD = 41e1153), reading all of media.py plus the media paths in tg_ingest_agent.py (4109–4600), fetch.fetch_json bounds, texts.py media keys, and CARA.md/SOLUTION.md.

CLEANLINESS OF THE CAPTION REVERSAL — clean. `media_card_hint_conflict` has zero references anywhere in the repo (code, texts.py, tests, docs); no orphaned template, test, or doc line survives. All 34 `media_*` keys defined in texts.py are reachable (several via the `"media_field_"+suffix` / `"media_src_"+pair[0]` / `"media_fname_"+suffix` concatenations). No half-applied weak-hint logic remains: `extract_prompt`'s hint text, `force_kind`, the post-force `dedup_entries` re-pass (tg_ingest_agent.py:4166), the `media_card_kind_forced` note and CARA.md:275-283 all describe the same authoritative behavior. `force_kind` is called exactly once, in `handle_media_capture` before enrichment, and never from `resolve_media_correction`, so it cannot clobber a later correction (with the caveat of finding #6, which is about the correction path's own field handling, not about forcing).

OWNER INVARIANTS — hold. No image path writes outside `tempfile.mkdtemp` + `shutil.rmtree` in `finally` (tg_ingest_agent.py:4121/4218-4221, covering success, decline and exception). Nothing is written before `_media_confirm` (`_media_merge_state` is read-only and deliberately does not create the category). Entries land as notes in English Movies/Books with RU titles verbatim. Provenance labels are structurally honest: every value carries a `_src` set at its source, `merge_preview` uses the separate `INHERITED_SRC` so a note's older value is never re-labeled photo or lookup, and I found no path where a looked-up value renders as photo-sourced.

BOUNDEDNESS — holds. `fetch_json` is called only via `_lookup_json`, which is gated by a per-batch `_LookupBudget` (10 calls, fail-fast on 2 consecutive transport failures) and `LOOKUP_MAX_BYTES=256KB`, `LOOKUP_TIMEOUT=5` with `DEADLINE_FACTOR=2` → 10s wall-clock per call, so the module docstring's "10 × 10 s ≈ 100 s" worst case is still accurate. Remote JSON is parsed defensively throughout: `isinstance` guards on every container, `str()` on every scalar, `docs[:5]` / `subjects[:20]` / `pages[:3]` slices, and a None return from `_lookup_json` never reaches an attribute access.

NEUTRALIZATION — holds. Every value that survives a lookup passes `_clean_line` (`common.neutralize_fences` + whitespace flattening + cap) before entering the `_model_fill` prompt (`json.dumps` of already-flattened single-line values), the card, or `entry_facts`. Year is re-gated by `_YEAR_RE` and genre by the fixed `_GENRES` table, so free remote prose cannot become either. I probed prefix forgery (a lookup creator or photo comment containing `"photo: author: …"`): `_CATALOG_FACT_RE` is `^`-anchored so the outer provenance prefix always wins — no forgery, though see finding #8 for an ordering hazard d31f2ba introduced.

THE REAL DAMAGE is concentrated in d31f2ba's same-title disambiguation (`_candidate_score` / `_strong_context_terms` / `_select_context_candidate`), which fails in BOTH directions: one high-severity path where it confidently picks a wrong same-title work, and three paths where it vetoes a correct one. Plus a negated-remove parse bug and one correction-path regression that d31f2ba created by adding photo-sourced structured fields without updating an existing call site.

FLOW-INVARIANTS REVIEW of `41a5818..HEAD` (d31f2ba + 41e1153) over `handle_media_capture` / `_stage_media_card` / `_resolve_media_merges` / `_media_merge_state` / `_media_store_entries` / `_media_confirm` / `handle_media_callback` / correction path / album path.

WHAT VERIFIED CLEAN (mechanical checks the assignment asked for):

1. NO photo is ever stored, on any path. `grep` for `insert_image|insert_file|media_dir|download_file` across `tg_ingest_agent.py` returns ZERO hits inside the media-capture flow (lines 4109-4586). The only fetch is `_download_photo_tmp` (4223-4243), which writes exclusively into `tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cara-photo-")` (4121) and is torn down by `shutil.rmtree(tmpdir, ignore_errors=True)` in a bare `finally` (4218-4221). That `finally` covers every exit: `return False, None` (4132), the media-branch `return True, None` (4153, 4201), the document/other returns (4208-4211), the `except llm.BudgetExceeded` branch (4212-4217), and any unexpected exception (e.g. a `TelegramError` out of `reply`). Confirmed correct.

2. NOTHING is written before consent. Every call in the card-drawing path is a read: `_media_merge_state` uses `store.canonical_category(self.conn, name) or name` (4393) — NOT `ensure_category`, exactly as claimed; `media.catalog_index` (4395) and `store.message_facts` (4400) are SELECTs. `self.note_no(merge["row_id"])` (4372) reaches `store.ensure_note_no`, which writes only when `note_no IS NULL` — and `store.confirm_category` (store.py:2482) assigns it, so a confirmed catalog note always already has one. The only pre-consent writes are the kv stash (`kv_set`, 4299) and the pending slot (`pending_set`, 4302), which are the documented staging mechanism. `store.ensure_category` appears exactly once, at 4529, inside `_media_store_entries` — i.e. after the confirm boundary. Confirmed correct.

3. Card-time and confirm-time category strings cannot diverge: `ensure_category` returns `canonical_category(name)` when the category exists and the raw `name` otherwise (store.py:1699-1712), which is bit-for-bit what `_media_merge_state` computes. So a merge resolved against `Movies` at card time cannot be stored against a different `Movies` at confirm time.

4. The reversal of d31f2ba's weak-hint design is CLEAN. `media_card_hint_conflict` is deleted from `texts.py` and has ZERO remaining references in any `.py` or `.md` file in the repo; the golden template list (`test_assistant.py:19962-20005`) was updated to match; `extract_prompt` no longer contains any "evidence wins" language for the kind; `CARA.md:274-290` and the `SOLUTION.md` media row both describe the authoritative-caption behavior and mention the weak hint only as dated history. No half-applied weak-hint logic remains fighting `force_kind`.

5. `merge_preview` is display-only and cannot inherit twice or mislabel: it reads `entry.get(f)` and never writes into the entry (media.py:1090-1097); the preview lives under `e["merge"]["fields"]` which `_resolve_media_merges` recomputes from scratch on every render (4410-4419); no code path copies `merge` back into the entry's own fields; an inherited value always carries `INHERITED_SRC` («уже в записи»), never `photo`/`lookup`.

6. Single-pending-slot discipline is intact. `slot_ours` (4282) prevents stealing a foreign slot; `_media_confirm` (4500-4502) and `handle_media_callback` (4583-4585) only clear the pending when it is still `media_capture`; the unconditional `pending_clear` in `resolve_media_correction` (4470) is safe because `dispatch` (1906) only reaches that method when the pending IS `media_capture`. Double-confirm is safe (stash consumed at 4499 before any write). The `"redrawn"` sentinel is handled correctly by both callers (2071 truthy check, 4578 toast).

RESIDUAL FINDINGS: 11 below, none of them a violation of the "no photo stored" or "nothing before consent" decisions. The two most consequential are correction-path gaps that 41e1153 fixed for `force_kind` but did not back-port to the reply-correction path.

Scope: the caption-authority reversal (d31f2ba's weak hint + `media_card_hint_conflict` → 41e1153's authoritative `media.force_kind`) and the CARA.md / SOLUTION.md media sections at HEAD.

VERIFIED CLEAN (no findings):
- The reversal is mechanically complete. `media_card_hint_conflict` has ZERO references at HEAD — texts.py, media.py, tg_ingest_agent.py, test_assistant.py, CARA.md, SOLUTION.md, the plan doc. The golden template test `test_media_templates_format_in_both_languages` (test_assistant.py:19962) was updated in the same commit: the old key is gone from `cases`, `media_card_kind_forced` was added, so an orphan key would be caught. No `action_truth.py` registration existed for it (only `media_saved` is registered there); nothing else to unwire.
- No weak-hint logic survives. `extract_prompt` (media.py:125-146) now states the hint is AUTHORITATIVE and there is no residual "visible evidence wins" branch; the only remaining `kind_hint` plumbing (tg_ingest_agent.py:4141) feeds that prompt, and the result is overridden post-extraction by `force_kind` regardless of what the model answered, so a model that ignores the hint cannot fight it.
- Ordering is correct: `force_kind` (tg_ingest_agent.py:4158) → conditional re-`dedup_entries` (4166) → `enrich_entries` (4171) → card. The lookups therefore run under the caption's kind, and `force_kind` calls `clear_enrichment` (media.py:370) BEFORE flipping, so a book's photo/lookup «author» cannot resurface as «режиссёр» (covered by test_movie_caption_outranks_the_book_shaped_cover and test_book_caption_outranks_a_film_poster_and_looks_up_a_book, which assert the negative fact `lookup: author: …` / `director:` respectively).
- A per-entry correction after a forced card WINS: `force_kind` is called only inside `handle_media_capture`; `resolve_media_correction` (4440) and the `_media_confirm` redraw path (4497) re-stage without re-forcing, so «№1 — книга» after a «Фильм» caption is not clobbered.
- CARA.md's only surviving "weak hint" sentence (line 277) is explicitly marked historical («Previously it was a weak hint…»), and the D4-invalidated justification was rewritten honestly in both docs and in the tg_ingest_agent.py comment at 4375-4382 (the invariant is now backed by card-time merge preview + confirm-time re-check, and CARA.md states the same).
- Batch-wide forcing IS stated in both specs («the kind is forced on every extracted entry», «applies it to every entry») — see the low finding below about the card-side disclosure, not the docs.

Findings below are ordered by severity; the first two are the substantive ones.
